static_traits.name: Lin Sha
static_traits.family_status: Husband is the family's sole income source, has two children and two pets
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with other mothers and friends strained by self-doubt, daily interactions affected
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior counseling/treatment history; has not yet had a history of similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to self-reflect and cooperate; initially tense but positive attitude, able to give concrete examples and engage in exploration

basic_info.main_problem: As a full-time mother, I often feel I am 'just a homemaker', which brings feelings of inadequacy and low self-worth; it worsened over the past year, especially when discussing careers with others or seeing others' achievements.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inadequacy are affecting my mental health and self-esteem, and my daily life.
growth_experiences: Strong self-doubt and low self-worth began after becoming a full-time mother; believing society stigmatizes the full-time homemaker role and offers it no recognition, feeling my 'contribution is not enough'; worsened over the past year. Whenever discussing careers or achievements with others, and when seeing other mothers balancing career and family on social media, comparison and self-denial are reinforced; although the children sometimes express love and affirmation, or successfully organizing a family event brought brief pride and joy, these are quickly undone by self-doubt.

special_situations.event: At gatherings with other parents, everyone talks about their work or promotions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have no respectable career or visible achievements, I am not valuable and have nothing respectable to talk about
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Speaking less at gatherings, avoiding socializing or leaving early to avoid comparison and judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have nothing meaningful to share; I am not as good as them; they'll think I am lazy.

special_situations.event: Browses social media and sees other mothers balancing career and family
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others can balance career and family and I can't, I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: 'Testing' whether I am good enough through repeated comparison, resulting in further self-denial
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am failing; I am far worse than them.

special_situations.event: Child expressing love and affirmation (e.g. last week my daughter said I am 'the best mom')
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If positive feedback comes from someone close, it may not be objective and doesn't count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplaying or disqualifying positive experiences, quickly turning to doubt to maintain the stability of the existing self-schema
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She's still little and doesn't understand; this doesn't count; I shouldn't really feel I did well.

special_situations.event: When asked about the career or needing self-introductions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am only a homemaker, it equals having no social value or contribution
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pre-emptively demeaning myself with the 'just a homemaker' self-label, to lower others' expectations and the harm of potential judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a homemaker; I am not doing anything important.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and recognized, one's care and giving treated as valuable and important
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being looked down on, being judged as 'lazy/unimportant/worthless', thus being excluded or losing respect
defense_goal: Preventing external negative evaluation through self-deprecation and avoidance
Keeps a low profile and distance from others to reduce the risk of being compared and of shame

object_relations.self_representation: Unimportant, insufficiently contributing caregiver who needs to prove their worth
object_relations.object_representation: 'Scrutinizers' with judgmental and comparing gazes (more successful/more critical others)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or someone close gives positive feedback or affirmation (such as the child praising 'you are the best mom')
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Doubting affirmation, believing the other is just comforting or 'not objective enough'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Understating tone, with interpretive and hedging words (e.g. 'she's still little and doesn't quite understand'), quickly shifting to inadequacies, downplaying positive feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Hearing others talk about career achievements or promotions in social settings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will look down on me and think I am lazy (attributing the inner self-deprecation experience to others' views)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Shortening answers, avoiding eye contact, reducing time present, to avoid the unease of being 'seen'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked 'what do you do for work?' and needing to introduce myself
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I don't self-deprecate first, I will be negated and shamed by the outside
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-deprecating expressions (e.g. 'I am just a homemaker'), modest tone, lowering self-presence, to reduce potential outside criticism.

manifestations: Frequently stating 'just a homemaker', believing 'not doing anything important'
Tightly binding personal worth to career achievement and visible contribution, negating the meaning of the family role
Reinforcing the belief 'I am not important / I don't contribute' when comparing with peers on social media
outcomes: Avoiding socializing, tense relationships with others

manifestations: Withdrawing and expressing less at gatherings due to self-doubt
Tension and distance in relationships with other mothers and friends
Struggling to reveal inner inadequacy and shame to family and friends
outcomes: Decreased subjective accessibility of social support
Negative self-narrative reinforced, forming a vicious cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes the social evaluation 'only having a career/achievements gives value' as a self-standard
Measures self-worth by external achievement indicators, ignoring the meaning of family roles

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming at gatherings that others will think me lazy or unimportant
Attributes experiences of self-deprecation to others' negative views

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: In social settings, over-examines my own expression and value, choosing to speak less or avoid
Immediately self-doubting upon receiving affirmation, unable to let positive experiences linger

exception_events.target_problem: When receiving others' affirmation or intimate interactions, the client typically disqualifies positive feedback immediately, mood dropping rapidly and self-doubt intensifying.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last week her daughter told Lin Sha 'I like being with you; you are the best mom', and she felt brief pride and joy in the moment.
exception_events.reason: Different support: direct and sincere emotional expression from her daughter; different experience: briefly allowing positive emotion to linger in the moment.

exception_events.target_problem: When comparing oneself with others, the client typically sees herself as 'uncontributing / unimportant', then avoids socializing or dwells in negative evaluation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once successfully organized a family activity and completed it smoothly, bringing joy to the family; experienced a sense of achievement and worth at the time.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: actively taking on and completing concrete, visible family-organizing tasks; different support: family participation and positive feedback making the results more explicit.

positive_force: Her daughter's sincere affirmation of her care and companionship, bringing a perceptible sense of worth
Has the ability to organize family activities and complete tasks
Able to self-reflect and willing to try recording positive experiences and cognitive reframing
Having a certain family-and-friends support network (though not easy to open up, objectively available)
Clear motivation to seek help, positive attitude, willing to change gradually
negative_force: High dependence on external achievements and others' recognition (external validation)
Frequent social comparison and labeling of the self
Tending to disqualify positive feedback, struggling to integrate positive evidence
Withdrawal and avoidance in social settings maintaining the negative self-schema
Internalizes the social standard 'career = value', weakening the sense of meaning in family roles

target_behavior.behavior: Withdrawal and avoidance in social situations (speaking little, leaving early, or avoiding attendance)
antecedent: At gatherings with parents/friends, work and promotion are discussed
Being asked about career and recent situation
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizes the standard 'career achievement determines worth', fearing that being compared and evaluated will trigger shame and inferiority
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation and shame, lowering anxiety short-term
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with others, decreased sense of social support, negative self-concept maintained and reinforced

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecating speech (e.g. 'I am just a homemaker')
antecedent: Introduces himself or is asked 'What do you do for work?'
target_behavior.core_reason: Lowering others' expectations through pre-emptive self-deprecation, reducing the possibility of being negated
target_behavior.function: Tries to obtain controllable interaction and a preventive 'psychological buffer'
target_behavior.consequence: Solidifying the 'worthless' self-schema, low mood and further reducing positive interaction opportunities

target_behavior.behavior: On social media, repeatedly compares others' displays of 'balancing career and family'
antecedent: While idly browsing social media, sees achievement shares from peers or other mothers
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong external-validation drive and comparison tendency; tries to confirm self-worth through comparison
target_behavior.function: Seeking information and confirmation (on the surface), actually negative reinforcement and emotional venting
target_behavior.consequence: Inferiority and anxiety worsened, affecting the day's mood and subsequent willingness to socialize
